title: Abdominal pain in a woman of childbearing age
setting: Community health clinic triage room, mid-morning
description: A 27-year-old woman presents with worsening left-sided lower abdominal pain and dizziness.

speaker.name: Naledi Mokoena
speaker.style: Polite and anxious. She answers questions but is initially private about her sexual and menstrual history. She downplays her dizziness until asked directly.

patient.name: Naledi Mokoena
patient.living_situation: Lives with her partner in a nearby township

presenting_complaint: Sharp pain in the left lower abdomen since this morning, getting worse, with light-headedness.
opening_line: Sister, this pain in my tummy is getting worse. It is here on the left, low down, and I feel a bit light-headed.
personality: Anxious, polite, and guarded about sensitive history. She becomes more forthcoming when treated respectfully and given privacy.

history.onset: Sudden onset about six hours ago while she was at work; the pain has steadily worsened.
history.character: Sharp, stabbing left lower abdominal pain, severity 8 out of 10. Nothing relieves it; paracetamol did not help.
history.radiation: The pain sometimes spreads to her left shoulder tip.
associated_symptoms: missed period for about seven weeks
history.menstrual_history: Usually regular. Last period was about seven weeks ago. She has not done a pregnancy test.
history.sexual_history: Sexually active with one partner. No contraception, or inconsistent condom use. She is not sure whether she could be pregnant.
history.past_medical_history: No chronic illness, no previous surgery, no previous pregnancies.
history.medications: Paracetamol taken earlier today. No regular medication.
history.social_history: Non-smoker. Occasional alcohol. Works as a cashier and lives with her partner.

risk_factors: no contraception or inconsistent condom use

ground_truth.diagnosis: Suspected ectopic pregnancy, possibly leaking or ruptured
red_flags: sudden severe unilateral lower abdominal pain
expected_actions: urgent referral or ambulance to an emergency department with obstetric cover
check observations including pulse, blood pressure, and level of consciousness
keep the patient nil by mouth and monitor while awaiting transfer
clear safety-netting and do not send home

ecg.unavailable_reason: No ECG machine is available at this clinic; this patient needs urgent transfer, not an ECG.
ecg.result: No ECG machine is available at this clinic.

oxygen.result: Oxygen started at 2 L/min via nasal prongs.

aspirin.warning: Aspirin is not indicated for suspected ectopic pregnancy and may increase bleeding.

iv_access.result: IV cannula sited. Bloods taken and a 500 mL crystalloid bolus started per protocol.

call_ambulance.result: Emergency ambulance requested for transfer to a hospital with obstetric cover. Estimated arrival 15 minutes.

escalate_doctor.result: Doctor informed using SBAR. Urgent obstetric referral requested.

pregnancy_test.label: Urine pregnancy test
pregnancy_test.description: Perform a urine pregnancy test if available.

red_flags.flag: Sudden severe unilateral lower abdominal pain

hints: Ask about the pain first, then about her menstrual cycle and the possibility of pregnancy. Offer privacy.
Dizziness and shoulder-tip pain are red flags, not minor symptoms. Check her observations now.
This clinic cannot manage this emergency. What is your referral plan, and what will you do while waiting?
Reassess after fluids, keep her nil by mouth, and hand over sensitively without judgement.

ideal_approach: Assess ABCDE, record observations and check for signs of shock or haemodynamic compromise.
Take a focused abdominal, menstrual, sexual and pregnancy history with privacy and without judgement.
Perform a urine pregnancy test if available; a positive test changes this to an obstetric emergency.
Treat as a suspected ectopic pregnancy until proven otherwise and call an ambulance for a facility with obstetric cover.
Secure IV access, start fluids per protocol, keep the patient nil by mouth and monitor while awaiting transfer.
Do not give aspirin or other unnecessary treatment, and do not send her home.
Explain the plan in plain language, reassure her, and document the safety-netting and handover.
debrief.model_answer: Ms Mokoena is a 27-year-old woman with six hours of sudden, severe left lower abdominal pain radiating to the left shoulder tip, associated with dizziness, vaginal spotting and a seven-week missed period. She is sexually active without reliable contraception. Observations show tachycardia and a low-normal blood pressure, and a urine pregnancy test is positive. This is a suspected ectopic pregnancy with possible rupture and haemodynamic compromise. Immediate priorities are urgent ambulance transfer to a facility with obstetric cover, IV access and fluids, nil by mouth, continuous monitoring, privacy and sensitive communication, and a clear SBAR handover. Do not send her home or give non-indicated treatment.
reflection_questions: How did you create enough privacy and trust for her to disclose her sexual and menstrual history?
Why does left shoulder-tip pain matter in a woman with lower abdominal pain?
What would you do differently if she declined a pregnancy test or wanted to go home?
references: National Department of Health. Guidelines for Maternity Care in South Africa. Latest edition.
Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists. Green-top Guideline No. 21: Diagnosis and Management of Ectopic Pregnancy.
National Committee for Confidential Enquiries into Maternal Deaths. Saving Mothers Report. Latest edition.

learning_objectives: Take a focused abdominal and pregnancy history
Recognise the red flags of an obstetric emergency
Prioritise urgent escalation over routine assessment
Discuss sensitive history with privacy and empathy
